subject: PrivDeploy IaC: dependency contract and release criteria
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@blueridge.io>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: PrivDeploy IaC: dependency contract and release criteria

Hi team —

Attaching a first-pass "dependency contract" and a short release-criteria draft for private deployments (VPC + on-prem). Goal is to lock down what counts as a module-level contract between infra teams (TF/Helm/Ansible), and what CI gates are required before we mark a module "production-ready" for a customer VPC/on-prem rollout.

High-level asks:
- Quick read of the PDF (iac-dependency-contract-v1.pdf) and the release criteria doc (release-criteria-v1.md).
- For infra owners: confirm which checks can be automated in GitLab CI (plan/diff, OPA policy, image provenance, helm lint, ansible-lint).
- For networking: list required network prerequisites for an "approved" module (subnet ranges, firewall-rule template, SR-IOV assumptions).
- For security/compliance: required evidence artifacts to attach to the release (SBOM, signed OPA policy eval, scan reports).

Proposed minimal gating (draft):
1) Terraform: fmt + validate, plan-only in CI with drift check; a plan review step for non-trivial changes.
2) Helm: lint + schema validation; values set for air-gapped/online modes; image policy verified.
3) Ansible: lint + idempotence tests in a small sandbox; inventory gating.
4) Common: OPA policy pass, unit tests for helper modules, small integration smoke-run in staging using a curated fixture.

Deadline: please respond with comments or ack/no-ack by EOD Wednesday so we can iterate before the Nov 10 customer readiness cutoff.

Attachments: iac-dependency-contract-v1.pdf, release-criteria-v1.md

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Deploy Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@blueridge.io>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: dependency contract and release criteria

Vivek — thanks for pulling this together. Quick inline thoughts below.

> Proposed minimal gating (draft):

Terraform:
- +1 on plan-only in CI for all PRs. We should require a "plan approved" label for any change that touches networking or bootstrap modules.
- Add: terraform-docs validation in the pipeline to keep interface docs up to date (helps downstream owners).

Helm:
- Helm schema is good but we need explicit values templates for the two supported distribution modes (online, air-gapped). Put those in helm-values-guidelines.md (attached).
- For image provenance: require signed image metadata (cosign) OR registry allow-listing. The gating should fail if images are pulled from an external registry unless explicitly allowed.

Ansible:
- For idempotence: we should run ansible-playbook --check in a small VM inside our sandbox runner. Works for most modules but network/firmware tasks will need manual approval.

Common:
- OPA policy evaluation must be part of merge checks. We should add a remediation playbook link in the contract so reviewers can suggest quick fixes.
- For evidence artifacts: SBOM for any container image, plus a small runbook demonstrating rollbacks.

Two additional asks:
1) Add an explicit "module deprecation" clause: how we indicate in the contract that a module will be removed and who owns the migration path.
2) Define a "fast-fail" list (things that require immediate rollback and a postmortem) vs. "soft-fail" (deprecated defaults that can be changed later).

I've attached helm-values-guidelines.md with a short template. I'll follow up with a small PR that wires terraform-docs and cosign checks into the runner.

Irene
Senior Infra Engineer, Deploy Runtime
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: helm-values-guidelines.md

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@blueridge.io>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy IaC: dependency contract and release criteria

Couple of network-specific constraints that need to be explicit in the contract: 
- Subnet templating: modules must accept CIDR overlays (no hard-coded /24 assumptions).
- Firewall rule templates: require both "allow list" and "deny by default" examples; provide a minimal recommended rule-set for common ML infra (NTP, NTP, metrics, model-store ports).
- SR-IOV and NIC passthrough: mark any module that requires SR-IOV as "hardware-ops" and gate it behind a manual sign-off (we cannot automate SR-IOV validation in CI).
- VLAN/segmentation: include a sample mapping doc for customers with restricted VLAN ranges.

Marissa: can you confirm the needed telemetry hooks (SNMP/Prometheus metrics endpoints) so we can include them in the release criteria? Also tagging: modules should emit a "redwood.module.name" label for inventory.

Short ack from me on the contract once the firewall template is in.

Grace
Network Lead, Deploy Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@blueridge.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T16:24:00-08:00
Subject: FW: PrivDeploy IaC: dependency contract and release criteria — BlueRidge feedback

Hi all —

FW: my notes after reviewing the attachments and running a quick compliance pass against our customer's checklist. Short summary: the contract is a solid baseline. A few items we can help automate on our side if you want:

- We can add a small policy-enforcer job that runs cosign verification and pushes SBOMs into the signed-artifacts bucket.
- We recommend adding a "contract matrix" doc that maps modules -> required artifacts -> gating job name. I created a draft at the Confluence link you already have.
- For network gating, we can provide a small harness that validates CIDR templating and runs firewall rule simulation using the customer's ACL samples. That would give you an automated preflight check before human sign-off.

Next steps I propose:
1) Accept v1 of the dependency contract as a living doc (merge with the caveat we will update the matrix).
2) Add 2 CI jobs in the CI runner: "artifact-signing" and "network-preflight". BlueRidge will PR templates for both.
3) Schedule a 30-min sync with hardware-ops to walk SR-IOV manual sign-off flow (Nov 6 or Nov 9).

I've uploaded the BlueRidge template PR to the shared Drive and linked a Confluence checklist in the related links. Happy to take point on the initial PR if you want me to.

Regards,
Alex Taylor
Principal Consultant
BlueRidge Systems
alex.taylor@blueridge.io
